mainTopic: The broken-strap sandal and רבי יוחנן's view, פנים חדשות for repaired utensils, and the permitted knots on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a distinction: an item that still works for its purpose stays a כלי, but a sandal with a broken outer strap does not. The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה from a סתם משנה about a sandal whose ears broke. רב יצחק בן יוסף answers by reading that משנה as a four-eared sandal. רבין then reports that רבי יוחנן ruled against רבי יהודה, and the גמרא explains that different אמוראים transmitted רבי יוחנן's view differently. Next, רבי חזקיה asks whether small sealed holes in a utensil add up to the pomegranate-size hole that makes it טהור. רבי יוחנן answers from his teacher's own sandal ruling: פנים חדשות באו לכאן, so a heavily repaired item counts as a new object. רבי חזקיה praises him, and the גמרא adds a saying about the greatness of earlier generations. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה's list of permitted knots on שבת. For each item it asks פשיטא and answers with a case of two openings, a pattern that continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: There it is still usable, but here it is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes distinguishing the other case from ours. There the item still functions for its purpose. Here, with the outer strap broken, the sandal does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that for its own purpose it is still a utensil. But here, for its own purpose, it is not a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began on the previous amud. It explains why the other case stays a כלי while our sandal does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item stays a כלי, and keeps its טומאה, as long as it can still do its own job. In the other case the object can still be used for its purpose. A sandal with a broken outer strap cannot be worn, so רבי יהודה rules it טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: for its own purpose / its own function

phrases.english: that for its own purpose it is a utensil,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא — לְמִילְּתֵיהּ לָאו מָנָא הוּא.
phrases.english: but here, for its own purpose, it is not a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא לְמִילְּתֵיהּ לָאו מָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a distinction begun on the previous section of the daf
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases seemed comparable, so both should have the same status
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether the item can still serve its own purpose. Our sandal cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the guiding principle for the whole sugya: טומאה depends on whether the item still works as a כלי for its intended use.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really rule like רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה. He holds that הלכה follows a סתם משנה. A סתם משנה about a sandal with one broken ear seems to make no distinction between inner and outer straps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה. And we learned: a sandal one of whose ears broke and was repaired remains טמא מדרס. If the second ear broke and was repaired, it is pure from conveying מדרס, but it is impure with מגע מדרס. Doesn't this mean there is no difference between the inner and outer strap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה. It uses his own rule that a סתם משנה is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סתם משנה says that when one ear breaks, the sandal stays טמא מדרס, and it does not say which ear. That implies even a broken outer ear leaves it טמא. This contradicts רבי יהודה, who says a broken outer strap makes it טהור, so רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: an unattributed משנה, stated with no named author
impure with the severe טומאה of a זב's treading
a lighter טומאה from contact with a מדרס item

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהור מלטמא מדרס' does not mean fully pure. It loses the severe מדרס status but still carries the lighter מגע מדרס טומאה.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
the halacha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned: a sandal one of whose ears broke
and he repaired it, is impure with treading-impurity;
if the second broke and he repaired it,
it is pure from conveying impurity as treading-impurity,
but it is impure through contact with treading-impurity.
Is it not that there is no difference whether inner
or outer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution to רבי יוחנן of the ruling like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה. That משנה implies a broken outer ear does not make the sandal טהור, which contradicts רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The משנה means only the inner strap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סתם משנה speaks specifically about the inner strap breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is specifically the inner one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by limiting the משנה to a broken inner strap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יהודה agrees that a sandal with a broken inner strap stays טמא. If the משנה only discusses the inner strap, it does not argue with רבי יהודה at all, and the contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: No, specifically the inner one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, פְּנִימִית דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the משנה's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers any ear, inner or outer
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only the inner strap, where רבי יהודה agrees it stays טמא

steps.title: Then the משנה should have made that distinction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer. If a broken outer strap makes the sandal טהור, the משנה should have said so directly within its own case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the outer strap, is it then pure? If so, instead of teaching 'if the second broke and was repaired it is pure from מדרס but impure with מגע מדרס,' let it distinguish within the case itself: when was this said? When the inner strap broke. But if the outer strap broke, it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3. It argues that the משנה would have spelled out such an important distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a broken outer strap makes the sandal fully טהור right away, that is a bigger and more obvious difference than the second-ear case. The משנה should have taught the inner versus outer distinction instead of moving on to a second ear. Its silence suggests no such distinction exists.

keyTerms.meaning: let it distinguish within that same case
in what case was this said?

phrases.english: But the outer one, what? It is pure?
If so, instead of teaching:
if the second broke and he repaired it,
it is pure from treading-impurity
but impure through contact with treading-impurity,
let it distinguish within the case itself:
in what case were these words said?
when the inner one broke;
but the outer one — it is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה refers only to the inner strap
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the inner versus outer distinction were real, the משנה would have taught it directly instead of discussing a second ear.

steps.title: Read the משנה as a sandal with four ears
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בן יוסף reinterprets the משנה as a sandal with four ears and four straps. 'The second' then means the second outer ear, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is preserved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בן יוסף said: let our משנה be about a sandal with four ears and four straps, so as not to break the words of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בן יוסף gives a new reading of the משנה. Its purpose is to save רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two outer ears, one broken outer ear still leaves the sandal wearable, so it stays טמא even according to רבי יהודה. Only when the second outer ear breaks does it lose its מדרס status. The משנה now fits רבי יהודה, though the גמרא openly admits this reading is adopted to protect רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: so as not to break (contradict) his words

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a claim about ordinary sandals. It is a forced reading of the משנה, admitted as such, made to keep רבי יוחנן consistent.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak ben Yosef said:
Let our mishna be about a sandal
that has four ears
and four straps,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁבּוֹר דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: so as not to break the words of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּהֵא מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ בְּסַנְדָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אׇזְנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 with a new case setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a normal two-eared sandal, so 'second ear' includes the outer one
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a four-eared sandal, and the second ear refers to the second outer ear
steps.whatToRemember: To keep רבי יוחנן consistent with his rule of following a סתם משנה, the גמרא reads the משנה as a four-eared sandal. This lets the משנה agree with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבין's report: רב follows רבי יהודה, רבי יוחנן does not
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. He also reports that רבי יוחנן ruled the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רב חנן בר אבא, who said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report arrives from ארץ ישראל. It presents רבי יוחנן's view as the opposite of what we assumed until now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the sugya assumed רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה. רבין's report flips that, and it sets up a new contradiction with everything above.

keyTerms.meaning: when רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Ravin came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Abba said that Rav said:
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
the halacha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a competing report of רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן: it does not.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן explained things according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבין's report. רבי יוחנן himself gave an explanation in line with רבי יהודה's view, so it seems he agrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? From the fact that רבי יוחנן explains in line with רבי יהודה, learn from it that he holds like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבין's report. It points to the earlier discussion, where רבי יוחנן was treated as holding like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from רבי יוחנן's own conduct. He took the trouble to explain things in line with רבי יהודה, which suggests he holds like רבי יהודה. רבין's report that he rules against רבי יהודה cannot easily fit with that.

keyTerms.meaning: from the fact that he explains

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But from the fact that Rabbi Yochanan explains
according to Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: learn from it that he holds like Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָא מִדִּמְתָרֵץ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבין's report using the earlier discussion
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's report that רבי יוחנן rules against רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Explaining things according to רבי יהודה shows that רבי יוחנן agrees with him.

steps.title: Different אמוראים reported רבי יוחנן differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two different אמוראים disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are different אמוראים, disagreeing about the view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. It says these are two different traditions about רבי יוחנן's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן did not contradict himself. One אמורא understood him as ruling like רבי יהודה, which is the basis of the earlier discussion. Another, the source of רבין's report, understood him as ruling against רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: The two conflicting rulings of רבי יוחנן are not a contradiction in his own view. They are two different אמוראים' reports of what he held.

phrases.english: They are different amoraim
and (they disagree) according to Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמוֹרָאֵי נִינְהוּ וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן himself said two contradictory things
steps.terutzMaskana: Two אמוראים transmitted רבי יוחנן's view differently

steps.title: The pomegranate-size rule for homeowners' utensils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת כלים: an impure utensil belonging to an ordinary homeowner becomes טהור once it has a hole the size of a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: for all utensils belonging to homeowners, the measure that makes them pure is a hole the size of pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a known rule from another משנה so it can ask a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner does not throw out a pot just because it has a small hole. He patches it and keeps using it. So the utensil stays a 'utensil', and stays טמא, until the hole is so big (pomegranate-size) that it is no longer usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Pomegranate, used here as a measure of hole size

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
All utensils of homeowners,
their measure (to become pure through a hole) is the size of pomegranates.
phrases.notes: The utensil leaves its impure status only once a hole this large makes it useless.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic connected to the sandal discussion in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A homeowner's utensil becomes טהור only when it has a hole the size of a pomegranate.

steps.title: Small sealed holes that add up to a pomegranate
steps.stepSummary: רבי חזקיה asks about a utensil that got several olive-sized holes, each sealed before the next one formed, until all of them together equal a pomegranate-sized hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חזקיה asked: suppose the utensil got a hole big enough for an olive to fall through, and he sealed it. Then it got another olive-sized hole, and he sealed that too. This continued until the holes together added up to a pomegranate-sized opening. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חזקיה asks a real question. Do the small, already-patched holes add up to make the utensil טהור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is never one open pomegranate-sized hole at any moment, because each hole was patched before the next one appeared. The question is whether the total damage counts, or only the damage that is open at one time.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question of law)
It was pierced or got a hole
A hole large enough for an olive to fall out

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥizkiya asked:
If it was pierced with a hole large enough for an olive to come out, and he sealed it,
and then it was pierced again with an olive-sized hole, and he sealed it,
until the holes added up to a pomegranate-sized opening, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about an unusual case under the pomegranate rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do several small holes, each sealed in turn, combine to reach the pomegranate measure and make the utensil טהור?

steps.title: The student reminds his teacher of the sandal case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reminds רבי חזקיה of his own teaching about a sandal. If one ear broke and was fixed, the sandal stays טמא מדרס. If the second ear then broke and was fixed, it is טהור from מדרס but still טמא מגע מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Master, you taught us this. If one ear of a sandal broke and the owner fixed it, the sandal is still impure with מדרס impurity. If the second ear broke and he fixed it too, the sandal is pure from מדרס impurity, but it is still impure as something that touched a מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts answering his teacher. He brings a parallel case that רבי חזקיה himself had taught: a sandal damaged in two separate stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sandal case has the same shape as the holes case: damage happens step by step, and each step is repaired before the next. Even so, after the second repair the sandal loses its מדרס status. This suggests that separate, repaired pieces of damage can add up.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'ear' (loop) of the sandal that holds the strap
Impure as a primary source because a זב stepped or sat on it
A lesser impurity from having touched a מדרס item

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהור מן המדרס' does not mean fully pure. The sandal loses only its strong מדרס status. It is still impure at a lower level, because it touched itself while it was still a מדרס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
Master, you taught us
that if one of a sandal's ears broke and he fixed it,
it is still impure with treading (מדרס) impurity.
If the second ear broke and he fixed it,
it is pure from treading impurity,
but it is impure as something that touched a מדרס.
phrases.notes: At the moment it stopped being a מדרס, it was touching itself while still a מדרס.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי, שָׁנִיתָ לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to רבי חזקיה's question by bringing a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether small, sealed holes add up to the pomegranate measure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חזקיה's own teaching on the sandal with two ears broken and fixed one after the other.

steps.title: The students' old challenge on the sandal ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן recalls that the students once challenged the sandal ruling. After the first break the sandal stays impure because the second ear is still whole. But after the second break, the first ear is already fixed, so why should the result be different?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked you: why is the first break different? Because the second ear is still standing. But at the second break, the first ear is already repaired!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן retells the question the students asked back then. It sets up the key principle his teacher gave in reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At every moment only one ear is broken, because the other one is either whole or repaired. So the two moments look the same, and logically the sandal should stay impure the second time too. This challenge pushes toward a new kind of reason.

phrases.english: And we asked you:
What is different about the first break, that it stays impure?
Because the second ear is still intact?
At the second break too, the first ear is repaired!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן לָךְ: מַאי שְׁנָא רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the students' challenge to the sandal ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the sandal becomes טהור מן המדרס after the second ear is broken and fixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both breaks look the same, since only one ear is ever broken at a time. So the second break should not change the sandal's status any more than the first did.

steps.title: A new object: the principle of פנים חדשות
steps.stepSummary: רבי חזקיה had answered that פנים חדשות בָּאוּ לְכָאן: once both ears have been replaced, it is a new sandal. רבי יוחנן says the same applies to the utensil whose many sealed holes add up to a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: 'A new face has come here.' Here too, with the utensil, a new face has come here.
steps.whatsHappening: This step finishes רבי יוחנן's answer. He takes his teacher's principle from the sandal and applies it to the utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sandal is טהור after the second repair, not because of how much is broken at one moment. It is because so much of it has been replaced that it is no longer the original impure item. In the same way, a utensil patched until the patches total a pomegranate is a 'new' utensil, and the old impurity is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: And you told us about it
A new face has come here: it counts as a new object

steps.whatToRemember: פנים חדשות בָּאוּ לְכָאן: when enough of an item has been repaired or replaced, it counts as a new object and the old impurity falls away. רבי יוחנן uses this to answer that the small sealed holes do add up to a pomegranate.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of פנים חדשות shows that what can count is the total change to the object over time, not only the damage visible at a single moment.

phrases.english: And you told us about it:
'A new face has come here' (it is a new sandal).

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן.
phrases.english: Here too (with the patched utensil), a new face has come here.
phrases.notes: So the utensil is טהור once the patched holes add up to a pomegranate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרְתְּ לַן עֲלֵיהּ: פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the old challenge and applies it to רבי חזקיה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The holes do add up. Through פנים חדשות, the heavily patched utensil is a new item and becomes טהור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a new principle (a new object) that explains the difference between the first and second break.

steps.title: The teacher praises his student
steps.stepSummary: רבי חזקיה is amazed by רבי יוחנן's answer. One version says he called him 'not a human being' (meaning an angel). Another version says he called him 'a true human being'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said about him: 'This is not a human being!' Some say he said: 'This is what a human being should be!'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story moment. The teacher praises his student for answering a question by using the teacher's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions are high praise. The first says רבי יוחנן's understanding is above human, like an angel. The second says he is the ideal of what a person can be.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a human being (he is like an angel)
This is a model human being

phrases.english: He exclaimed about him:
'This is not a human being!' (but an angel)
Some say he said:
'Someone like this is a true human being!'

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ: לֵית דֵּין בַּר אִינָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records רבי חזקיה's reaction to רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חזקיה praised רבי יוחנן either as more than human or as the ideal human being.

steps.title: Earlier generations compared to later ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רבא בר זימונא: if earlier generations were like angels, we are like people. If they were like people, we are like donkeys, and not even special donkeys, just ordinary ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבא בר זימונא: If the earlier generations were like children of angels, we are like children of people. If the earlier generations were like children of people, we are like donkeys. And not like the donkey of רבי חנינא בן דוסא or the donkey of רבי פנחס בן יאיר, but like regular donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related saying about how great earlier generations were compared to later ones. It fits the praise just given to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying sets a scale: whatever level the earlier generations reached, we are one big step below them. The famous donkeys of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and רבי פנחס בן יאיר were known to be unusually wise, so the speaker says we are not even like those.
steps.whatToRemember: The section ends with a lesson of humility: later generations should respect how great the earlier חכמים were.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר זִימּוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rava bar Zimuna said:
If the earlier generations are like children of angels,
we are children of people.
And if the earlier generations are like children of people,
we are like donkeys.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כַּחֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
phrases.english: And not like the donkey of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa
or that of Rabbi Pinḥas ben Yair,
phrases.notes: Both donkeys were famous for unusual, almost wise behavior.

phrases.english: but like ordinary donkeys.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר זִימּוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the praise of רבי יוחנן with a general teaching about the decline of the generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each later generation is far below the earlier ones, one full level lower.

steps.title: Why mention wine and oil skins? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to tie wine and oil skins and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one may tie wine and oil skins. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of permitted knots and challenges one item as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knots on wine and oil skins are opened all the time to pour out the liquid. So they are clearly temporary knots and clearly permitted on שבת. The question is: why did the משנה bother to list this case?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a ruling is too simple to need saying)

steps.confusionAlert: פְּשִׁיטָא does not argue with the ruling. It agrees with the ruling and only asks why the משנה had to state it.

phrases.english: And [the Mishnah said one may tie] wine and oil skins.
phrases.notes: A quote from the list of permitted knots in the משנה.

phrases.english: That is obvious!
phrases.notes: They are opened all the time, so the knot is clearly temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story about רבי יוחנן and רבי חזקיה and returns to the משנה's list of knots.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to list wine and oil skins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A knot that is opened all the time is clearly not a permanent knot. So listing it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a skin with two openings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a skin with two spouts. We might have thought one spout is tied for good, but the משנה teaches it is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the skin has two spouts. You might have said: he gives up on one of them and leaves it tied for good. So the משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question. It shows a case where the ruling is not obvious at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a skin has two spouts, the owner could pour from just one of them. Then the knot on the other spout might be treated as permanent, and a permanent knot is forbidden on שבת. The משנה teaches that we do not assume this: both knots count as temporary and are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (the case is limited to show why the ruling is needed)
You might have said... (the mistaken first thought)
He gives it up, leaving it tied for good
So it teaches us (the real ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: This pattern (פְּשִׁיטָא, then לָא צְרִיכָא, then מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, then קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן) repeats for each item in the rest of this passage.

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ תַּרְתֵּי אוּנֵּי,
phrases.english: It is needed only where it has two ears (spouts),

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: חֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ בַּטּוֹלֵי מְבַטֵּל לַהּ,
phrases.english: You might have said: one of them, he gives it up (leaving it tied for good),
phrases.notes: That would make it a permanent knot, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: So it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ תַּרְתֵּי אוּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פְּשִׁיטָא by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two spouts, one knot might be given up and become permanent, so it would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with two spouts, neither knot is treated as permanent, so tying is permitted.

steps.title: Why mention a meat pot? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to tie a cover over a pot of meat and asks why this was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one may tie [a cloth over] a pot of meat. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list and asks the same 'obvious' question. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloth tied over a pot has to be untied whenever someone takes food out. So it is clearly a temporary knot. Again the question is why the משנה had to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary knot, which is permitted on שבת

phrases.english: [And the Mishnah said:] a pot of meat.
phrases.notes: One may tie a cloth over it.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same challenge as step 16 on the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to list a meat pot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cover must be opened to take out food, so the knot is clearly temporary.

steps.title: The case is a pot with another way to open it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a pot that has a שְׁלָאכָא, a second way to get at the food. We might have thought the main knot is left tied for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where it has a שְׁלָאכָא. You might have said: he gives up on the knot and leaves it tied for good. So the משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question about the pot, using the same kind of answer it gave for the wine skins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pot has another way to take out the food, the owner might never untie the main cloth. Then that knot would look permanent and be forbidden. The משנה teaches that it is still a temporary, permitted knot.

keyTerms.meaning: A string or flap that gives another way to open the pot and take out food
A permanent knot, which is forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: It is needed only where it has a string (another opening),
You might have said: he gives it up (leaving the knot tied for good),
So it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לַהּ שְׁלָאכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פְּשִׁיטָא of step 18 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there is another way in, the main knot might be left alone for good and count as permanent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The knot is still treated as temporary and is permitted.

steps.title: Why mention רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rope? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling that one may tie a rope in front of an animal, and asks why it was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: one may tie it [a rope in front of an animal]. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last item in the משנה and asks the same 'obvious' question. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rope tied across a doorway so an animal will not get out is untied whenever people or animals pass through. So it is clearly temporary. Why did רבי אליעזר בן יעקב need to state this?

keyTerms.meaning: One may tie it (here, a rope in front of an animal)
Etc.: the quote is cut short

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר קוֹשְׁרָהּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: one may tie it, etc.
phrases.notes: In the משנה: one may tie [a rope] in front of an animal so it will not go out.

phrases.english: Isn't that obvious?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same challenge on the third item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rope across a doorway is opened all the time, so it is clearly a temporary knot.

steps.title: The case is a doorway with two ropes
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a doorway with two ropes. The 'you might have said' part begins here and is finished on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where it has two ropes. You might have said... (continued in the next section).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer about the rope, using the same pattern as before. The sentence breaks off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two ropes across the doorway, a person might use only one and leave the other tied for good. That would make the second knot permanent and forbidden. The full mistaken thought and the ruling (קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן) come on the next amud.
steps.whatToRemember: All three items follow one pattern. Each case has two openings or two ropes. We might think one knot is given up and becomes permanent (forbidden). The משנה teaches that each knot stays temporary and permitted.

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לַהּ תַּרְתֵּי אִיסָּרֵי,
phrases.english: It is needed only where it has two ropes,
You might have said...
phrases.notes: This continues on the next amud, just like the earlier cases: one of them he gives up, so the משנה teaches that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לַהּ תַּרְתֵּי אִיסָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פְּשִׁיטָא of step 20 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two ropes, one might be left tied for good and count as a permanent knot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Finished on the next amud: the knot is still temporary and permitted.
